prs.title: chore(release): engine 0.2.4 and desktop 0.2.15
prs.body:
## For users
Engine and kit packages report 0.2.4, and the desktop app reports 0.2.15.

Integrators: no breaking changes since 0.2.3. `sx project-settings` and the `projectDefaults` request option are new, and the kit now ships every setting's default. Read the `sx-core` and `@slicerx/mcp` 0.2.4 changelogs for the rest.

prs.title: fix(settings): read a PrusaSlicer project's 0% shrinkage as no shrinkage
prs.body:
## For users
PrusaSlicer projects open at their real size and slice again. A project with a nonzero shrinkage compensation opens without it, and the open note says so.

Effective config from the app's open path, main against this branch, for the 2.9.6 fixture and a T slab saved in 2.9.6. Only these keys change:

| Setting | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| `filament_shrink` | [0] | [100] |
| `filament_shrinkage_compensation_z` | [0] | [100] |
| `initial_layer_infill_speed` | [0] | [100] (50% of the 200 mm/s infill speed) |

Each config, sliced by the CLI on the default printer (256 x 256 mm plate):

| File | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| prusaslicer-2.9.6.3mf | refused, part 2000 x 2000 mm | 100 layers |
| prusaslicer-2.9.6-tslab.3mf | refused, part 3000 x 800 mm | 90 layers |

prs.title: fix(core): iron each object on its own filament inside the layer's tool order
prs.body:
## For users
Multi-filament plates with ironing now keep each part on its own filament. On main, an A1 plate with a 5 mm box on filament 1 and a 20 mm box on filament 2 printed the 20 mm box from 5.2 mm up on filament 1. The same happened on P1S, X1C and H2D projects, with or without the prime tower and with support on or off. Plates without ironing, or printed by object, print as before.

Moves, E and speeds are byte identical. Only the `;HEIGHT:` lines and the preview's segment heights for those beads change.

prs.title: fix(core): zero first-layer and support widths, overhang wall width
prs.body:
## For users
First-layer and support widths set to 0, and overhang walls, now print at the right width.

Filament per mm by feature, main against this branch, from our own G-code (feature labels as written). MK4 and Ender-3 V3 KE are the shipped profiles. The "zero" setups use outer 0.42, inner 0.45, internal solid 0.42, first layer and support at 0, and line width 0.48 (MK4) or 0.42 (Ender). L1 is the first layer. Cube is a 20 mm cube, ledge is a 24 mm slab hanging 16 mm off an 8 mm pillar.

| Setup | Part | Feature | main | branch | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MK4 | cube | all | | | same file |
| MK4 | x-mark | Overhang wall | 0.029097 | 0.029404 | +1.1% |
| MK4 | ledge, bridge flow 1 | Overhang wall | 0.029098 | 0.031227 | +7.3% |
| MK4 | ledge, bridge flow 0.8 | Overhang wall | 0.023278 | 0.031227 | +34.2% |
| Ender | cube | all | | | same file |
| Ender | x-mark | Overhang wall | 0.029098 | 0.030736 | +5.6% |
| Ender | ledge, bridge flow 1 | Overhang wall | 0.029097 | 0.031924 | +9.7% |
| Ender | ledge, bridge flow 0.8 | Overhang wall | 0.023277 | 0.031924 | +37.2% |
| MK4 zero | cube | L1 outer wall | 0.033173 | 0.030729 | -7.4% |
| MK4 zero | cube | L1 bottom surface | 0.033172 | 0.030729 | -7.4% |
| MK4 zero | ledge | L1 inner wall | 0.033175 | 0.033175 | 0.0% |
| MK4 zero | ledge, support | L1 support | 0.033171 | 0.035616 | +7.4% |
| MK4 zero | ledge, support | Support | 0.037290 | 0.044439 | +19.2% |
| MK4 zero | ledge, support | Support interface | 0.039626 | 0.048996 | +23.6% |
| MK4 zero | ledge, bridge flow 1 | Overhang wall | 0.029098 | 0.032323 | +11.1% |
| MK4 zero | x-mark | L1 outer wall | 0.033174 | 0.030729 | -7.4% |
| Ender zero | cube | L1 outer wall | 0.033173 | 0.030729 | -7.4% |
| Ender zero | ledge, support | L1 support | 0.033171 | 0.030726 | -7.4% |
| Ender zero | ledge, support | Support interface | 0.042045 | 0.044566 | +6.0% |
| Ender zero | x-mark | L1 bottom surface | 0.033172 | 0.030727 | -7.4% |

Every other feature is within 0.2% of main. Support layers use their own heights here (`independent_support_layer_height` is on), so the whole-print support numbers mix layer heights; the tests below check support at 0.2 mm layers exactly. Total filament on the x-mark moves by 0.1 to 0.5 mm. On the zero-width ledge with support it goes from 374.9 to 403.9 mm (MK4) and 365.8 to 372.6 mm (Ender).

Bambu Lab output is byte-identical to main for stock profiles, which set `initial_layer_line_width` to 0.42 (checked below). A Bambu Lab project file that leaves `initial_layer_line_width` out now reads it as unset, the same as 0, so its first-layer lines and first-layer support print at their own feature widths instead of one shared width. Those projects may see different first-layer and support widths after this change.

prs.title: fix(core): run sparse hooks to the tip of a narrow tongue
prs.body:
## For users
- Tapering parts no longer leave an empty strip down the middle where sparse infill starts, with inner walls narrower than the stock width or with three or more walls.
- Filament: +0.24 % to +0.34 % on the affected parts we measured (+0.26 % with 0.40 mm inner walls, +0.34 % with 0.55 mm inner walls, +0.24 % with three walls). Every stock project opens byte for byte as on main, so 0 % there.
- Still open:
  - With four walls, a strip that ends at the wide end of a part before any sparse line enters it (part widths 3.66 to 3.91 mm on the test wedge, up to 3.9 mm of part empty). The hook needs a line end to start from, and there is none there.
  - Tongues longer than five anchor lengths (about 8 mm) keep their last stretch empty: 1.0 to 1.4 mm on the test wedge, with 3 or 4 walls and inner walls of 0.35 to 0.38 mm.
  - The spot where the strip is still narrower than one sparse line, about 0.3 mm of part, stays as before.

Layer counts on a 20 mm cube (a cone for the C, A and S rows), main against this branch. P1S and A1 profiles: maximum 0.28 mm, minimum 0.08 mm. Ender-3 V3 profile: maximum 0.35 mm, minimum 0.10 mm. "Ender-3 V3 at 0.24" is the same profile with its maximum set to 0.24 mm. First layer 0.2 mm unless the row says otherwise.

| Printer | Case | main | This branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1S, A1 | Layer 0.30 | 72 (0.28 mm) | 67 (0.30 mm) |
| P1S, A1 | Layer 0.32 | 72 (0.28 mm) | 63 (0.32 mm) |
| P1S, A1 | Layer 0.36 | 72 (0.28 mm) | 56 (0.36 mm) |
| P1S, A1 | Cone, layer 0.32 (plain, adaptive key, sleipnir quality) | 72 (0.28 mm) | 63 (0.32 mm) |
| P1S, A1 | First layer 0.32, layer 0.32 | 71 (0.32, then 0.28 mm) | 62 (all 0.32 mm) |
| P1S, A1 | Object layer 0.32, plate 0.20 | 72 (0.28 mm) | 63 (0.32 mm) |
| P1S, A1 | Layer 0.05 | 248 (0.08 mm) | 397 (0.05 mm) |
| P1S, A1 | Layer 0.03 | 100 (fell back to 0.20 mm) | Refused: layer height 0.03 mm is below the 0.04 mm minimum |
| P1S, A1 | Layer 0.44 | Refused: bridge_line_width, a 0.400 mm line is not wider than the 0.4 mm layer | Refused: layer height 0.44 mm cannot exceed the 0.4 mm nozzle diameter |
| Ender-3 V3 | Layer 0.38 | 58 (0.35 mm) | 53 (0.38 mm) |
| Ender-3 V3 | Object layer 0.38, support off | Refused: support_line_width, a 0.380 mm line is not wider than the 0.38 mm layer | 53 (0.38 mm) |

| Ender-3 V3 at 0.24 | Layer 0.32 | 83 (0.24 mm) | 63 (0.32 mm) |

Unchanged on every printer: layer 0.20 and 0.12, layer equal to the maximum (0.28, 0.35), first layer above the maximum with 0.20 layers, object layer 0.12, and every height range case.

prs.title: fix(core): slow arachne overhang walls by the share of their own bead
prs.body:
## For users
On arachne walls, overhangs start slowing at a smaller lean, about 8.8 degrees on a 0.42 mm wall at 0.2 mm layers (the classic curve starts near 13). The slowdown now comes in finer steps that follow each bead's real width. With the stock A1 and P1S overhang speeds, the first slower step is at 20 degrees (162.5 mm/s), where the classic curve held 200 until 23 degrees. Print time goes up slightly on leaning parts. On our 31-wedge stock A1 sweep the estimate went from 52m 16s to 52m 37s.

Slicing time against main, 7 interleaved base/new rounds of 5 projects, release build, median wall time per slice (1-minute load 25.6 to 27.9 at round start):

| Project | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 31 wedges, stock A1 | 0.083 s | 0.083 s |
| 71 wedges, knots far apart | 0.161 s | 0.164 s |
| 66 wedges, 0.25 degree steps | 0.139 s | 0.137 s |
| 44 wedges, three wall loops | 0.132 s | 0.131 s |
| 48 thin leaning plates | 0.122 s | 0.120 s |

The differences are within run-to-run spread.

prs.title: fix: read the Bambu Studio project defaults from one shared table
prs.body:
## For users
Compared with main, one case gets worse in time: a Bambu Studio project that never names a prime tower wall, sliced in the app or through the MCP server, now prints the rib tower, as it already did through `sx slice`. On the test project (P1S, two filaments, tower on) the tower goes from about 34.6 x 11.8 mm (rectangle) to about 24.5 x 24.1 mm (rib), and the estimate goes from 1h28m58s to 1h34m38s.

Integrators: Bambu Studio projects with no tower wall key now slice with the rib tower through the MCP server and the app, as they do through `sx slice`. `sx project-settings <file.3mf>` prints the settings a project slices with, `slicerx_inspect_project` returns them as `project_config`, and requests can opt in with `"options": {"projectDefaults": true}`. Request clients should take `config` from one of these instead of the raw project JSON.

prs.title: perf(voronoi): write FixedInt products straight into the result, and time two more stages
prs.body:
## For users
Slicing is about 1.5 to 2% lighter on CPU, with the same G-code. The timing report now has internal bridge and seam plan stages.

Integrators: `stageMicros` gains two keys, `bridges` and `seams`. Code that reads known stage names is unaffected, and code that sums every key now counts these two as well.

prs.title: fix(gcode): acceleration for wipes and layer-end travels
prs.body:
## For users
On the A1 and A1 mini, the lift and the moves to the timelapse park position now run at the travel acceleration instead of the print acceleration. Wipes on every printer now run at the layer's default acceleration, not the last path's.

Most prints change by a few seconds against main: the A1 x-mark goes from 1h 13m 16s to 1h 13m 3s, and the A1 two-color x-mark from 3h 3m 9s to 3h 2m 45s. An A1 with every acceleration set to 3000 gets slower (13m 39s to 13m 56s on a cube), because its paths after the head wrap check now run at the 3000 the person set instead of the template's 5000.
